abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>
                  In breeding programs, the selection of cultivars with the highest yield potential consisted in the selection of the yield
                  <jats:italic>per se</jats:italic>
                  , which resulted in cultivars with a higher grain number per spike (GN) and occasionally higher grain weight (GW) (main numerical components of the yield). This task could be facilitated with the use of molecular markers such us single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP). In this study, quantitative trait loci (QTL) for GW, GN and spike fertility traits related to GN determination were mapped using two double haploid (DH) populations (Baguette Premium 11 x BioINTA 2002 and Baguette 19 x BioINTA 2002, BP11xB2002 and B19xB2002). Both populations were genotyped with the iSelect 90K SNP array and evaluated in four (BP11xB19) or five (B19xB2002) environments. We identify a total of 305 QTL for 14 traits, however 28 QTL for 12 traits were considered significant with an R
                  <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                  > 10% and stable for being present at least in three environments. There were detected eight hotspot regions on chromosomes 1A, 2B, 3A, 5A, 5B, 7A and 7B were at least two major QTL sheared confident intervals. QTL on two of these regions have previously been described, but the other six regions were never observed, suggesting that these regions would be novel. The R5A1 (
                  <jats:italic>QSL.perg-5A, QCN.perg-5A,QGN.perg-5A)</jats:italic>
                  and R5A.2 (
                  <jats:italic>QFFTS.perg-5A, QGW.perg-5A)</jats:italic>
                  regions together with the
                  <jats:italic>QGW.perg-</jats:italic>
                  6B resulted in a final higher yield suggesting them to have high relevance as candidates to be used in MAS to improve yield.
                </jats:p>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Author contribution statement</jats:title>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Key message</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    28 stable and major QTL for 12 traits associated to spike fertility, GN and GW were detected. Two regions on 5A Ch., and
                    <jats:italic>QGW.perg-</jats:italic>
                    6B showed direct pleiotropic effects on yield.
                  </jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
